title: Anti-CD4 IgG Antibody Purification from HIV Plasma Samples
author: Luo, Jiang

The isolated anti-CD4 antibodies contain all classes of antibodies (e.g., IgA, IgM, IgG). Since IgG is the main class of antibodies presenting with ADCC activity, next we will isolate IgG from the anti-CD4 antibodies.➢Protein A IgG purification kit (Catalog number: 44667, ThermoScientific)➢Amicon Ultra-0.5 Centrifugal Filter Unit (Catolog number: UFC503096, Millipore)1.Remove the end write cover from the column.2.Insert the column into a 15 ml tube.3.Add 1 mL binding buffer to wash the column, perform 3 times, do not let the column dry completely.4.When column is almost dry, add 200–500ul plasma; let IgG bind to the column5.Add 1 mL binding buffer to wash the unbounded antibodies, perform 5 times.6.Add 1 mL elution buffer to wash the column; because the first wash buffer has the most IgG, the second wash can occur with 0.5 ml elution buffer.7.Add nanodrop to calculate protein concentration; wash nanodrop, add 2uL elution buffer to adjust for blank; add sample 2uL to measure protein concentration in the sample.8.To reuse the column, release all binding IgGs; add 1 mL elution buffer, perform 3 times to release the binding IgGs. Then add 1 mL binding buffer, l wash 3 times, leave 1 ml binding buffer; cap and store for future use.9.Next to concentrate IgGs and change buffer to PBS since elution buffer could impair IgGs.9a.Use Amicon Ultra-0.5 ml centrifugal filters 30k (IgG is about 150k)9b.Add the filter into a 2 ml vial provided in the kit9c.Add 0.5 mL isolated IgGs in elution buffer from step 8 to the column, then 14,000 g 10 min, repeat until all elution buffer uses.9d.Add PBS 0.5 ml, 14,000 g 10 min, 3 times9e.Reverse the column in a new tube, then centrifuge 1000 g for 2 min. This produces the concentrated IgGs, then add PBS to 0.5–1 mg/mL, aliquot and store at −80C to avoid repeated freezing and thawing.

1.Target cells (CD4+ T cells) and Effect cells (NK cells) obtained from non-immune responder HIV patients (undetectable plasma viral load, CD4+ T cell counts < 350 cells/µL) on antiretroviral therapy.Use the enrichment kit, strictly following the protocol provided in the kit.•EasySep™ Human CD4 Cell Enrichment Kit (STEMCELL, Catalog number: 19052)•EasySep™ Human NK Cell Enrichment Kit (STEMCELL, Catalog number: 19055)

This procedure is used for processing 250 µL – 2 mL of sample (up to 1 × 108 cells).A.Prepare a mononuclear cell suspension at a concentration of 5 × 107 cells/mL in the Separation Buffer. Cells were placed in a 4.5 or 5 mL polystyrene tube to properly fit into the Purple EasySep™ Magnet.a.Separation buffer: PBS PH7.2, supplemented with 0.5%BSA and 2 mM EDTAb.Falcon™ 5 mL Polystyrene Round-Bottom Tubes (BD Biosciences, Catalog number: 352058) or 4.5 mL polystyrene tubes (Catalog number: 120161, 4.5 mL PS tube, Greiner bio-one) are recommended.B.Add the EasySep™ Human CD4 or NK Cell Enrichment Cocktail at 50 µL/mL cells (e.g. for 2 mL of cells, add 100 µL of cocktail). Mix well and incubate at room temperature (15–25 °C) for 10 min.C.Vortex the EasySep™ D Magnetic Particles for 30 s. Ensure that the particles are in a uniform suspension with no visible aggregates.D.Add the EasySep™ D Magnetic Particles at 100 µL/mL cells (e.g. for 2 mL of cells, add 200 µL of magnetic particles). Mix well and incubate at room temperature (15–25 °C) for 5 min.E.Bring the cell suspension up to a total volume of 2.5 mL by adding separation buffer. Mix the cells in the tube by gently pipetting up and down 2 - 3 times. Place the tube (without cap) into the magnet. Set aside for 5 min.F.Pick up the EasySep™ Magnet, and in one continuous motion invert the magnet and tube, pouring off the desired fraction into a new 4.5 mL polystyrene tube. The magnetically labeled unwanted cells will remain bound inside the original tube, held by the magnetic field of the EasySep™ Magnet. Leave the magnet and tube in an inverted position for 2-3 s, then return to upright position.a.Do not shake or blot off any drops that may remain hanging from the mouth of the tube.b.From the following step, the separated NK cells should be kept at 4 °C, until the NK cells have been added in the 96 wells plate.G.Wash the cells with pre-cold separation buffer 2 times; the negatively selected, enriched cells in the new tube in R10 are now ready for use.

steps.title: Buffer exchange of sCD4
steps.instruction: Use an Amicon® Ultra‑0.5 mL centrifugal filter (10 kDa, Millipore, UFC5010) placed in the supplied microcentrifuge tube. Add 50 µL of recombinant soluble CD4 (sCD4, 1 mg/mL, amino acids 1‑370, CHO‑derived, >95 % purity, Progenics) to the filter, then add 400 µL 1× PBS. Cap and spin at 14,000 × g for ~7 min. Repeat the PBS spin two additional times. To recover the concentrate, invert the filter into a clean tube and spin at 1,000 × g for 2 min.

steps.title: Couple sCD4 to magnetic beads
steps.instruction: Follow the NHS Mag Sepharose (GE Healthcare, 28‑9440‑09) kit protocol using the NHS HP SpinTrap Buffer Kit (28‑9135‑69) and a Cytiva MagRack 6 (28948964).

substeps.instruction: Dispense 100 µL NHS‑activated magnetic beads into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube, place on the magnetic rack and discard the storage solution.
Add 500 µL ice‑cold equilibration buffer, resuspend gently, then remove the liquid.
Immediately add the sCD4 solution from Step 1, resuspend, and rotate end‑over‑end at 500 rpm for 60 min at 4 °C (or room temperature). Remove the liquid.

Block residual active groups by sequentially adding 500 µL of blocking buffer A, removing liquid, adding 500 µL blocking buffer B, removing liquid, adding 500 µL blocking buffer A, incubating 15 min with slow rotation, then adding 500 µL blocking buffer B, removing liquid, adding 500 µL blocking buffer A, removing liquid, and finally adding 500 µL blocking buffer B and removing liquid.
Add 500 µL binding buffer and remove the liquid to complete equilibration before use.

steps.title: Capture anti‑CD4 antibodies from plasma
steps.instruction: Use the sCD4‑coupled magnetic beads to isolate anti‑CD4 antibodies from plasma.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 µL of the labeled beads to a 50 mL conical tube. Add 20 mL plasma (containing anti‑CD4 antibodies) and 20 mL wash/bind buffer containing 2 M urea. Incubate with end‑over‑end rotation at 200 rpm for 4 h at 4 °C (or 2 h at room temperature).
Spin briefly at 10 g for 1 min, discard the supernatant (store if desired), and retain the bead pellet.
Wash the beads three times: add 500 µL wash buffer, mix, place on the magnetic rack, and discard the liquid each time.
Elute bound antibodies twice: add 500 µL elution buffer (2 M urea, VWR catalog 17‑1319‑01) per 50 µL bead volume, resuspend fully, incubate ≥2 min, then collect the eluate.

steps.title: Concentrate and buffer‑exchange antibodies
steps.instruction: Exchange the eluate into PBS and concentrate using Amicon® Ultra‑0.5 mL filters.

substeps.instruction: Insert a fresh Amicon® Ultra‑0.5 filter into a microcentrifuge tube. Add the 500 µL eluate, spin at 14,000 × g for ~5 min, and discard the flow‑through.
Repeat the spin until all eluate is retained on the membrane.
Add 400 µL 1× PBS, spin at 14,000 × g for ~5 min, discard flow‑through. Repeat the PBS wash two additional times.
Recover the concentrated antibody solution by inverting the filter into a clean tube and spinning at 1,000 × g for 2 min.

steps.title: Purify IgG using Protein A
steps.instruction: Isolate IgG from the total antibody preparation with a Protein A IgG purification kit (ThermoScientific, catalog 44667) and concentrate with a 30 kDa Amicon filter.

substeps.instruction: Remove the end‑write cover from the Protein A column and place the column into a 15 mL collection tube.
Wash the column three times with 1 mL binding buffer, avoiding complete drying.
Add 200–500 µL plasma (or the antibody preparation) to the column, allow IgG to bind.
Wash the column five times with 1 mL binding buffer to remove unbound proteins.
Elute IgG twice: first with 1 mL elution buffer, then with 0.5 mL elution buffer (the first elution contains the majority of IgG).
Measure protein concentration with a NanoDrop: blank with 2 µL elution buffer, then read 2 µL sample.
Regenerate the column for reuse by eluting bound IgG three times with 1 mL elution buffer, then washing three times with 1 mL binding buffer; leave 1 mL binding buffer in the column, cap, and store.

Concentrate and exchange the eluted IgG into PBS using Amicon® Ultra‑0.5 mL centrifugal filters (30 kDa cutoff, Millipore). Place the filter in a 2 mL vial, add up to 0.5 mL IgG eluate, spin at 14,000 g for 10 min; repeat until all eluate is processed.
Add 0.5 mL PBS, spin at 14,000 g for 10 min; repeat PBS wash three times.
Invert the filter into a fresh tube and spin at 1,000 g for 2 min to collect concentrated IgG.
Adjust IgG concentration to 0.5–1 mg/mL with PBS, aliquot, and store at –80 °C to avoid freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Enrich CD4+ T and NK cells
steps.instruction: Isolate CD4+ T cells and NK cells from patient PBMCs using EasySep kits.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a mononuclear cell suspension at 5 × 10^7 cells/mL in Separation Buffer (PBS pH 7.2 + 0.5 % BSA + 2 mM EDTA).
Add EasySep™ Human CD4 Cell Enrichment Cocktail (50 µL per mL of cells) and incubate 10 min at room temperature (15–25 °C).
Vortex the EasySep™ D Magnetic Particles for 30 s, then add 100 µL per mL of cells, mix, and incubate 5 min at room temperature.
Bring the volume to 2.5 mL with Separation Buffer, mix gently, place the tube in the EasySep™ Magnet for 5 min.
Invert the magnet and tube in one smooth motion, pour off the unlabeled (desired) fraction into a new 4.5 mL polystyrene tube; keep the tube inverted for 2–3 s before returning upright.
Wash the enriched cells twice with cold Separation Buffer; keep the NK cell fraction on ice (4 °C) until use.
Repeat the entire procedure with the EasySep™ Human NK Cell Enrichment Kit (same volumes and timings) to obtain NK cells.

steps.title: ADCC target‑cell depletion assay
steps.instruction: Measure CD4+ T‑cell killing by anti‑CD4 IgG in the presence of NK effectors.

substeps.instruction: Prepare CD4+ T cells in R10 (RPMI‑1640 + 10 % FBS) at 5 × 10^5 cells/mL. Dispense 50 µL (2.5 × 10^4 cells) into each well of a V‑bottom 96‑well plate.
Add anti‑CD4 IgG (final concentration 1, 2.5, or 5 µg/mL; titrate up to 10 µg/mL if needed) or control hIgG OKT3 (0.5 µg/mL). Incubate 30 min at 37 °C.
Prepare NK cells at 1.5 × 10^6 cells/mL in R10. Add 50 µL (7.5 × 10^4 cells) to each well (effector:target ratio = 3:1, total 1 × 10^5 cells per well).
Incubate the co‑culture 15 min at room temperature, then spin plate at 300 g for 1 min.
Incubate plates 6 h at 37 °C.
Stain cells with anti‑CD4 and anti‑CD3 antibodies, then with Annexin V (BD catalog 556454) in Annexin V binding buffer.
Acquire data on a flow cytometer within 30 min of staining.

steps.title: NK activation ADCC assay
steps.instruction: Assess NK activation markers after exposure to anti‑CD4 antibodies.

substeps.instruction: Dilute cells to 5 × 10^5 cells/mL in R10; add 50 µL (2.5 × 10^4 cells) of CD4+ T cells per well of a V‑bottom 96‑well plate.
Add anti‑CD4 IgG or control hIgG OKT3, incubate 15–30 min at 37 °C.
Dilute NK cells to 5 × 10^5 cells/mL in R10; add 50 µL (2.5 × 10^4 cells) per well of a U‑bottom plate (effector:target = 1:1, total 5 × 10^4 cells per well).
Add CD107a‑BV510 antibody (BD catalog 563078) at 2 µL per well, GolgiStop™ (brefeldin A, BD catalog 554724) and GolgiPlug™ (monensin, BD catalog 555029) at 1 µL/mL final concentration.
Incubate 15 min at room temperature, then spin at 250 g for 4 min.
Incubate plates 6 h at 37 °C.
Stain cells with Ghost Red 780 and anti‑CD3, then wash with 500 µL 1× PBS (350 g, 5 min) and vortex 5 s.
Fix/permeabilize: add 200 µL BD Cytofix/Cytoperm (catalog 51‑2090KZ) per tube, incubate 20 min on ice; prepare 1× BD Perm/Wash buffer (catalog 51‑2091KZ).
Add 300 µL Perm/Wash buffer, spin 450 g for 5 min, discard supernatant.
Add 2 µL anti‑IFN‑γ antibody, incubate 30 min at 4 °C protected from light.
Add 500 µL Perm/Wash buffer, spin 450 g for 5 min, discard supernatant; wash once more with Perm/Wash buffer.
Resuspend cells in 100–150 µL 2–4 % PFA (BioLegend catalog 420801), keep at 4 °C, and acquire on a flow cytometer.

description: After long-term antiretroviral therapy (ART) and peripheral viral suppression, up to 20% of people with HIV (PWH) fail to recover their CD4+ T cell counts to levels similar to healthy controls. CD4+ T cell decline characterizes these immune non-responders (INRs, aviremic/ART+, CD4+ T cell counts < 350 cells/mL); moreover, their CD8+ T cell counts are higher than healthy controls (1). We are the first group to report that plasma levels of anti-CD4 autoantibody IgGs are increased in INRs compared to immune responders (IRs) and uninfected controls, and purified anti-CD4 IgGs from plasma samples of INRs induced CD4+ T cell death through antibody-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC) in vitro (1–7). Notably, anti-CD4 IgG-mediated poor CD4+ T cell recovery from suppressive ART is the only mechanism targeting CD4+ T cells, specifically. Other known mechanisms (e.g., thymic and lymph node fibrosis, chronic immune activation, leaky gut, and increased microbial translocation) may not account for decreased CD4+ T cell counts specifically in INRs. Recently, there are studies and interests related to autoimmunity and anti-CD4 autoantibodies in HIV, though there is a debate about whether anti-CD4 autoantibodies mediate CD4+ T cell death through antibody-mediated cytotoxicity (8), which has conflicting results of our previous studies (1, 3, 9, 10)mainly due to the challenging technologies (antigen-specific antibody isolation from plasma and ADCC). To increase transparency and research reproducibility, we show methodology and explain the details of key steps in the anti-CD4 autoantibody isolation from plasma samples and the ADCC assay to allow reproducibility in the future. This protocol for isolating anti-CD4 antibodies also can be used to isolate any antigen-specific antibodies from plasma or from antibody containing fluids, using the desired antigens.
